clue.text: She hopes to sell her soul we hear

definitions.text: She hopes to sell her soul we hear

parts.words: She hopes to sell her soul we hear
parts.note: read as a pun: 'soul' said aloud is 'sole', the flatfish, so this woman's trade is selling fish at market, not a pact with the devil

explanation.surface: A woman who would trade her soul for a price, Faust-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'soul' into 'sole', the fish; the seller of fish is a market woman, famously loud-mouthed in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman selling fish from a stall is the literal sense; the word also means a coarse, shouting woman.

clue.text: Ziegfeld erected mast from remains of the wreck

parts.note: Florenz 'Flo' Ziegfeld, the Broadway impresario, gives his short first name

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the word upright reads it from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre producer puts up a ship's mast salvaged from a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'erected' stands the mast upright, so it reads from the bottom up. Ziegfeld's first name is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating debris and cargo left on the sea after a shipwreck is the classic sense.

clue.text: Insist on tulips with tea perhaps :

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters given might be arranged some other way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone demands tulips served with afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the nine letters of TULIPS and TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand something as a condition of an agreement is to lay it down firmly.

clue.text: On balance a sound way to cross a stream

indicators.note: 'a sound' tells us the letters entered are only how another word is pronounced

parts.note: to wade is to walk through shallow water to get across

explanation.surface: Advice that wading is a safe way to ford a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sound' makes the word WADE heard, spelt as the past tense of weigh, which rhymes with it exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something measured on scales has been placed on a balance, so 'on balance' describes that measuring.

clue.text: Miss Forsyte embraces an idle fellow

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: Fleur Forsyte is the young heroine of the later books of Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga

explanation.surface: A young lady of a famous fictional family hugs some layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' is the container signal. The Forsyte Saga is a British sequence of family novels, well known from television.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer strolling the streets with no purpose is the French-derived sense of this idler.

clue.text: Moslem city is one named for redevelopment

indicators.note: redeveloping a site rebuilds it in new form, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A city in the Islamic world has been earmarked for urban renewal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for redevelopment' rearranges I plus NAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saudi Arabian holy city where the Prophet is buried is Islam's second most sacred place.

clue.text: Kipling's Old Man, for instance (pocket edition)

definitions.text: Kipling's Old Man, for instance (pocket edition)

parts.words: Kipling's Old Man, for instance (pocket edition)
parts.note: Kipling's Just So Story features the Old Man Kangaroo; 'pocket edition' hints not at a small book but at the pouch such animals carry their young in

explanation.surface: A bibliographic note about a pocket-sized reprint of a Kipling story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocket edition' sounds like publishing jargon, but the pocket is the pouch of the kangaroo family.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo is the best-known pouched mammal, so the Old Man Kangaroo is one example of the group.

clue.text: He composed a small party in seed-raising

indicators.note: the party is placed inside the other piece
in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
Lib is short for the Liberal Party, a minor party in British politics

explanation.surface: A composer joins a minor political group devoted to plant cultivation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns SEED to DEES in this down clue, and 'in' splits it; 'seed-raising' poses as gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: Léo Delibes was the French composer of the ballet Coppélia and the opera Lakmé.

clue.text: This disarmament is mentioned in odd letters from Canada

definitions.text: This disarmament is mentioned in odd letters from Canada

parts.words: This disarmament is mentioned in odd letters from Canada
parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of Canada are C, N, D, the initials of the Campaign for this kind of Disarmament, whose middle word is wanted

explanation.surface: A news item: Canadian correspondence calls for disarmament.
explanation.walkthrough: CND, the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, is the British anti-bomb movement; its letters sit in the odd places of CaNaDa.
explanation.definitionFit: The campaign's initials stand for its full name, and the wanted word is the adjective qualifying 'disarmament'.

clue.text: He starts something, getting one drink into the speaker

indicators.note: the drink goes inside the speaker

parts.note: an orator is one who gives speeches
the Roman numeral for one is I
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble by plying a public speaker with liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who first creates or begins a scheme or idea is its founder.

clue.text: Thrash at this rate ?

definitions.meaning: to beat soundly, in a fight or a match
a speed, as in going 'at a fair' one

explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for beating an opponent, and also for a burst of speed, as in 'at full' pace.

clue.text: Inflation, deflated, once ruined many

parts.note: describes a historical speculative boom whose rising share prices collapsed, wiping out investors

explanation.surface: An economic warning that rising prices, once punctured, bring ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1720 collapse of a British trading company's inflated share price ruined many investors; 'inflation' and 'deflated' fit a bubble.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1720 share-price collapse of a company trading with South America is history's famous burst speculative mania.

clue.text: Wind River

definitions.meaning: to twist and turn, as a path does
a river in Turkey, the Büyük Menderes, known in classical times by this name

explanation.definitionFit: To wander in a twisting course is the verb, named after an Anatolian river famous for its loops.

clue.text: Explained how Ezra dived into river and died

indicators.note: a diver goes into the water, so the poet goes inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
Ezra Pound, the American poet
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A tale of a poet who plunged into a river and drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dived into' is the container signal; the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out the meaning of a text or theory in detail is to explain it.

clue.text: Change for a priest?

indicators.note: the clue's first word, read as a verb, says to alter the order of the following letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is coin for the collection plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges A PRIEST; read as a noun it is also coinage, which this old Middle Eastern currency unit is.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin and monetary unit of Turkey, Egypt and nearby countries is small money, so it is a kind of loose coin.

clue.text: Natural number

definitions.meaning: in pontoon or blackjack, a winning two-card hand of an ace and a ten-card

explanation.definitionFit: The top score in the card game pontoon is a 'natural' when dealt directly, and it is plainly also a whole number.

clue.text: With an internal knock they require treatment

indicators.note: the knock is placed inside the other word, so it becomes internal to it

parts.note: taken as written
a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: People who have taken a blow to the body need medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With an internal' is the container signal; 'require' is a link, and 'knock' suggests an injury, not a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Healing care for an illness or disorder, physical or mental, is a general synonym.

clue.text: Regular inclusion of a small piece in colour

indicators.note: including something takes it in, so these letters are held within
the piece goes inside the colour

parts.note: a hue is a colour or shade
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A routine of adding a small dab to some paintwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclusion of' and 'in' together signal the container; 'Regular' poses as an adjective but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A frequent visitor to a particular place, such as a bar, is a regular there.

clue.text: Chanticleer's masked flatterer so-called ?.

parts.note: in medieval beast fables the cock Chanticleer is flattered into singing by the fox, whose face looks masked, and the fox is given a traditional name

explanation.surface: A note on the deceitful courtier in a rooster's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The fox in Chaucer's version of the fable is called Russell, but the beast-epic fox is the masked creature known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional name of the fox in medieval European fables, so the cunning flatterer is so called.

clue.text: The opposite of a shut-down for a film star ?

definitions.text: The opposite of a shut-down for a film star

parts.words: The opposite of a shut-down for a film star
parts.note: 'shut down' and '...' look like synonyms, but for a star the phrase means a camera shot at short range

explanation.surface: A screen actor's career is in no danger of ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the phrase meaning 'shut down' is also the tight camera shot a star wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shot taken at very short range, showing the face in detail, is what a star hopes for.

clue.text: Opportunity beginner found in church

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
L stands for a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A novice's opportunity found inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir, stands for the church itself.

clue.text: How this' supervisor may ensure light work for the staff ?

definitions.text: How this' supervisor may ensure light work for the staff

parts.words: How this' supervisor may ensure light work for the staff
parts.note: a mine foreman's title, read as an instruction, hints at putting more people on a job than it needs so each has little to do

explanation.surface: A question about how a manager might ease employees' workloads.
explanation.walkthrough: Excess staffing makes light work for each person; the foreman's title echoes that.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreman or overseer, especially in a mine, is a supervisor of workers.

clue.text: What venal yes-men in part expect

definitions.text: What venal yes-men in part expect

parts.words: What venal yes-men in part expect
parts.note: corrupt flatterers want money for their compliance; 'in part' points to a part-settlement of what is owed

explanation.surface: A remark on what corrupt sycophants hope to receive.
explanation.walkthrough: Venal people can be bought, so they expect money; 'payment in part' is the stock phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Money handed over in return for a service is what a bribe-taker hopes for.

clue.text: Normandy's invasion record

parts.note: suggests the 1944 D-Day landings but means the embroidered chronicle of the Norman invasion of England in 1066, kept in a Norman town

explanation.surface: An archive document about the Second World War landings on the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invasion' tempts one towards 1944; the record here is the 11th-century embroidery showing William's conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: The long embroidered cloth depicting the 1066 Norman Conquest is housed in a town in Normandy.

clue.text: No end of ermine in the portico'

indicators.note: the last letter of the animal is taken off

parts.note: the ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: Endless ermine fur is displayed under a colonnade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' cuts the last letter from STOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered colonnade in ancient Greek architecture is a type of portico.

clue.text: Put out Crossways girl's chest-of-drawers

parts.note: Diana of the Crossways is a novel by George Meredith, and Diana shortens to Di, here with a possessive S
a commode is an ornate chest of drawers

explanation.surface: A girl's bedroom furniture is moved out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'girl's' supplies the S after DI.
explanation.definitionFit: To inconvenience or trouble someone is to put them out.

clue.text: Yielded, say, a better type of player

indicators.note: 'say' signals that the word is only spoken, so its sound is entered

parts.note: to cede is to yield or give up

explanation.surface: A sports player gave way, to put it one way, despite being a superior competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes CEDED heard. The definition describes a ranked player in a tournament draw.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis draws, players ranked above the rest are placed apart so they meet late, marking them as better.

clue.text: Like the clanger of a senior officer in the factory

indicators.note: the officer goes inside the factory

parts.note: a plant is a factory
GEN is the abbreviation for general

explanation.surface: A general blunders noisily on a visit to an industrial works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'clanger' suggests a blunder but here is a thing that clangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and resonant, with a reverberating ring, describes a bell's clang.
